markingScheme.criterion: Correctly names one of the five Pentagon of Health groups (Nutrition, Sleep, Exercise, Stress Management, or Community & Healthy Relationships).
markingScheme.accept: Any recognisable version of the group name, e.g. 'sleep' for Sleep Hygiene, 'being kind' or 'friends' for Community & Healthy Relationships.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague answer with no named group at all.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a real habit or food from their own Investigation Record that belongs to the named group.
markingScheme.accept: Any item the student actually sorted into that group during Investigate — check the Record table.
markingScheme.insufficient: An example that does not appear anywhere in the student's own logged results, or that belongs to a different group.

markingScheme.criterion: Names one genuine, plausible healthy habit from the student's own real life (not Pip's).
markingScheme.accept: Any believable everyday action for a 5-6 year old — eating a food, sleeping, playing, a hug, breathing calmly, etc.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly matches that habit to its Pentagon of Health group.
markingScheme.accept: Any of the five group names or a clear paraphrase (e.g. 'moving my body' for Exercise).

markingInstructions: This is a Primary 1 (age 5-6) activity — mark generously for age-appropriate spelling, phonetic spelling, and short sentences; never penalise spelling or grammar unless the meaning is genuinely unclear. Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using the point-by-point marking_scheme carried in each question's marking_context (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric's level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria beyond what is defined. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Use the raw Investigation Record data (not just the student's summary of it) to verify any claim the student makes about their own sorting results. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 60 words, written for a young child's parent/tutor.
